source.title: Does Momentum Change the Implicit Regularization on Separable Data?
source.authors: Bo-Han Wang; Qi Meng; Hui-Shuai Zhang; Ruo-Yu Sun; Wei Chen; Zhirui Ma; Tie-Yan Liu

record.tranche_reason: The study compares SGD and SGDM on a CNN using test accuracy, but does not test any listed claim version or measure the train–test gap.
record.gate_note: The paper's main results concern convergence to an L2 max-margin solution on separable linear classification problems, not held-out generalization gaps. The MNIST CNN experiment reports a qualitative comparison of test accuracy.
record.test_reason: The study analyzes optimizer convergence directions on separable linear classification and compares SGD with momentum SGD on MNIST. Neither measures a listed version. In particular, its Adam results concern max-margin convergence, not adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance required by V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate within the paper's assumptions: adding momentum preserves the studied asymptotic implicit bias for SGD and deterministic Adam in separable linear classification. The MNIST experiment reports similar SGD and SGDM test accuracy, with faster SGDM convergence. Extending the theory to deep networks and constant-learning-rate stochastic Adam remains future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper analyzes optimizer convergence and implicit regularization on separable linear classification; its CNN experiment compares SGD with SGDM rather than measuring generalization gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors state that convergence depends on suitable learning rates; the ill-posed synthetic dataset requires a smaller learning rate.

fits_no_version.finding: A four-layer MNIST CNN trained with momentum SGD achieves similar test accuracy to SGD and converges faster.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding momentum to SGD can preserve held-out accuracy while accelerating convergence in this MNIST CNN setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the stated separability, loss, and hyperparameter assumptions, GDM, SGDM, and deterministic Adam converge in direction to the L2 max-margin solution; stochastic RMSProp also does so with a decaying learning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: These optimizers share an asymptotic max-margin implicit bias in the studied separable linear classification setting.

record.problems: The MNIST CNN comparison is described qualitatively and its figure provides no textual numerical values in the supplied text; the experiment does not report a train–test gap.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification performance and local connectivity.
Adaptive-versus-SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning, weight-decay changes, or optimizer switching.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with generalization gaps, and comparison with other measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized versus random training examples.

record.verdict_notes: The absence of a reported train–test gap is not the decisive exclusion: V4 can be tested through held-out performance. Here, the held-out experiment lacks an adaptive optimizer, while the adaptive-optimizer experiments measure training accuracy and angular distance to the max-margin solution.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test generalization.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD held-out performance under the specified tuning conditions.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the train–test gap.
Effects of removing memorized training examples.
